Bad cop exposed

By: Viewfinder | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Did the South African Police Service enable a brutal murder by leaving this problem cop unchecked?

Unique Selling Point:
18 months long running investigation into repeat violent offender within SAPS, and SAPS management failure to discipline him. Backed up by a longer term investigation of the systemic use of torture and violence in police work in SA and failure of police accountability mechanisms in South Africa i.e. this case study is illustrative of a much deeper and systemic malaise within policing in SA

Summary:
Long term investigation has shown that alleged repeat violent offender within Western Cape SAPS, Sergeant Giovanni Gabriels, was left unchecked by SAPS management. He then led an operation during which a 36-year-old man was fatally assaulted, with witnesses saying Gabriels directed and participated in assault on Adam Isaacs. Documentation and records demonstrate how the officer was consistently shielded from disciplinary action by his superiors, in spite of findings against him.

Further information:
Full rendering of the characters, records available and investigative findings in this story is accessible via a long form article published by Viewfinder and News24: https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/viewfinder-did-saps-enable-a-brutal-murder-by-leaving-this-problem-cop-unpunished-20211201

Further angle: the officer has been transferred to a small community (Lambertsbaai) where his pattern of abuse has apparently continued.

Press Release:


Murder in police custody?
In January 2020, the army and police barged into Wasiela Isaacs' family home in Athlone, on the Cape Flats. The arrest of her son, Adam, ended with his death from blunt force trauma in hospital a few days later. Two years later, as Isaacs still waits for justice and closure, an investigation has revealed that one of the officers implicated in Adam's killing had a long history of unchecked brutality allegations against him.
Produced by Viewfinder | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli

Script:


Bad cop exposed
Commission number 6071
Script

Commentary
In July 2019, the army was deployed in the Western Cape to help police tackle gangsterism
on the Cape Flats. But, allegations of routine brutality in these joint operations soon
blemished the deployment.
In January 2020, 36-year-old Adam Isaacs from Athlone was arrested on suspicion of
drug-dealing during one such operation. Witnesses say that he was tortured for hours. Days
later, he died in hospital.
Today, Wasiela Isaacs, is still reeling from the loss of her eldest son.

Wasiela Isaacs
Adam, my son, he was a very clever, clever boy. He was always there for me. And, I miss
him so much now. It’s almost 2 years now. He passed away. The missing is still there. It’s still
there. Really, I really miss him.

MacFarlane Moleli
On the night that Adam was arrested, what do you remember about that night?

Wasiela Isaacs
The 26th of January, I will never forget. I went to the toilet, and all of a sudden I heard my
son calling “eina mammie help my. Mammie, eina help my”.
And I ran out of the toilet and I wanted to go. And, one of the soldiers said to me “waar gaan
jy”. I said “no man there Adam is calling me. They hit him there. He’s crying for his mommy”.
He said “no, no bly net hier binne, bly hier binne, jy gat n rens nie”. Ek s  “nee hulle slaat
my kind daar buite kant” .
And, they took Adam in the van, and they take him away. And, I don’t know what happened.
I was sick the whole night.

Link
After his arrest, Adam Isaacs was brought here to Groote Schuur hospital, under police
guard. His injuries were severe, but he clung to life for several days as surgeons tried to
save him.

Wasiela Isaacs
I was there by his bedside and I was praying and I was praying that night. That was the night
that he passed away. It was the 6th of February. Ten o’clock that night. (crying)

Commentary
Adam’s hospital file shows that his intestine had been ruptured. His muscles were breaking
down, releasing toxins into his bloodstream which, in turn, caused kidney failure. Later,
Adam’s post-mortem report concluded that he had died as a result of blunt force trauma
injuries.
Shamiel Gamieldien was one of those arrested in Athlone during the same operation. He
feels lucky to have escaped with his life, he says.

Shamiel Gamieldien
Daai was innie nag, toe het die polisie met die army opgetrek. Hulle het hier oorgespring.
Hulle het in gekom.
Translation: It was in the night, and the police and army pulled up here. They jumped over,
and came in here.
Gabriels en sy kollega wat ek persoonlik ken. Hulle was die mense wat hier in gekom het
saamet die army en vir my ges  het trek jou aan jy gaan gou saamet ons.
Translation: Gabriels and his colleague, whom I personally know. They said to me: “Get
dressed. You’re going to come with us quickly.”

Commentary
Police records show that Athlone sergeant Giovanni Gabriels was leading the police side of
the operation.

Shamiel Gamieldien
Hulle het my verdink aan smokkel. Daar van daan af, nou soos ons weer terugkom, Gabriels
het die baseball bat, en hy begin my te slat, en hy slat my arm gebreek. En sy kollega het ‘n
gun en hy slaat my agter my kop en agter my rug. Dis als op die doktor op die J88 gemerk.
They suspected me of (drug) smuggling. Now, as we came back, Gabriels had a baseball
bat and he started hitting me. He broke my arm. His colleague had a gun and he hit me
behind my head. [Mac: With the gun?] Yes, and on my back. It’s all marked on the doctor’s
J88 (legal document noting injuries).

Commentary
Shamiel’s case was but the latest in a long list of brutality allegations against Sergeant
Gabriels.
Nikkita Peters was just 18-years-old when, she says, Gabriels tackled her to the ground and
kicked her in the stomach as she tried to film him assaulting her cousin.
In June 2018, 60-year-old Veronica Franciscus accused Gabriels of storming her bedroom
and hitting her in the face, after arresting her son at home.
In April the following year, 53-year-old Nazeem Hardien accused Gabriels of tasering him
and pistol-whipping him in the face.
Yet, the most brutal allegation remains that he participated in the torture of Adam Isaacs.

Shamiel Gamieldien
Nou kan jy mos die windscreen sien. Nou sien ek hier, gebeur dinge voor my. Ek sien daar
het hulle vir Adam. Hulle begin vir Adam te slaat. Dis die army manne, en dis Gabriels hulle.
So muur, laat hulle hom daar teen aan staan. Dan kom hulle aan gehardloop, dan trap hulle
hom.
Now, one kan see through the windscreen. Now I see, here in front of me things are
happening. I see there they have Adam. They start beating Adam. It’s the army men, and it
is Gabriels and them. There was a wall like this, and they made him stand against it. Then
they came running up, and they stomped on him.
En soos hulle hom slaat, kom hulle terug na my toe en se jy’s next. (Praying) Allah help my.
And, as they are beating him, they came running back to me saying “you’re next.”
(Praying indistinctly)
I just said: “Allah help me.”

Shamiel Gamieldien
Daai kollega van Gabriels, hy’t so ‘n baksteen opgetel jong. A baksteen, hy konnie meer se
eina of so of se niks nie. Ek hoor hy gooi dit gwa teen daai man se rug.
That colleague of Gabriels, the white one, he picked up a brick. A brick. Adam, he couldn’t
say “ouch” or cry or anything. He could not feel it anymore. I just heard how he threw it
“Gwah!” against that man’s back.

Link
Watchdog records contain many brutality allegations against officers at Athlone police
station. Yet, complainants - such as the family of Adam Isaacs - say they have lost faith in
the station commander to discipline officers implicated in these cases.

Commentary
Following recommendations from the Independent Police Investigative Directorate, criminal
prosecutors are currently pursuing convictions in two separate counts of “assault with intent
to do grievous bodily harm” against Gabriels.
Yet, Athlone station commander Colonel Mark Adonis never gave Gabriels more than a
“warning”, in spite of repeat watchdog findings against him.
In the end, Adonis’ office also failed to investigate claims that Gabriels and other Athlone
officers participated in the torture of Adam Isaacs.
Sean Tait is the director of the African Policing Civilian Oversight Forum.

Sean Tait
Now, I’m familiar with the case of Sergeant Gabriels and the incidents in Athlone.

Sean Tait
You can say that it's part of the systemic failure within the South African police services
when it comes to discipline or when it comes to consequence management. Well we’ve seen
a steady decline In discipline cases being processed through the South African Police
Services.

Sean Tait
So a fraction resulting in any form of punitive sanction.

Commentary
Instead of disciplining and rehabilitating problem officers, Tait says that the police service
may simply transfer them to other precincts.

Sean Tait
When these transfers happen to more rural areas and more remote areas, you also
removing the individual from the scrutiny that might been available in a more kind
metropolitan or resourced area such as Cape Town.

Link
In 2020, the police service transferred Sergeant Giovanni Gabriels to this station in the quiet,
west-coast fishing village of Lamberts Bay. Here, some community members say, his pattern
of assault and abuse continued unchecked.

Commentary
Dawid Hendricks is a handyman at the Cederberg Municipality. He has accused Sgt Gabriels
of attacking him at his home in January last year.

MacFarlane Moleli
Dawid, just explain to me what happened that night that you say you were assaulted by
police. Take me through what happened?

David Hendricks
My vrou was geroep deur ‘n vriendin van haar… Haar kind is siek en sy het gegaan. Maar
dis Covid. Daai tyd was dit die Covid tyd. En sy het gegaan.
My wife was called by a friend, whose child was sick, and she went. It was Covid. It was
Covid time. But, she did go.
En sy het gebel vir my meisiekind, om te s  ek moet vir haar kom haal. Toe is dit al oor die
curfew-tyd.
And, she called my daughter to ask that I should come fetch her. Then it was already after
the curfew time.

Commentary
Dawid says that Gabriels and a colleague were patrolling his street to enforce curfew, when
they confronted him.

David Hendricks
En toe ek nou wil uitklim by my driver kant, hier ruk iemand die deur oop, voor my kombuis
deur, ruk hy die deur oop en hy het my in die kar. Ek vra ‘wat maak jy nou? Jy maak my
dood. Jy choke my.’ Ek wil opstaan. Ek wil uitklim. En hy is in die kar, hy maak my arms seer,
ek was dokter toe met my arms. Ek het ‘n J88. Dis ‘n hele vlamme hier op gewees soos hy
vir my seergemaak het.
En my drie kinders kom uit, my seun en twee meisiekinders kom uit. By die kombuis uit, dis
voor die deur. Hulle s  ‘Jy kan nie my pa in yard aanrand nie’. Alan Kotze vat die pepper
spray en hy spray al drie my kinders met die pepper spray.
And, when I wanted to get out at the driver’s side, someone pulled the door open. In front of
my kitchen door, he pulled the door open and he had me in the car. I asked him “What are
you doing? You are killing me! You are choking me!” I wanted to stand up. I wanted to get
out. And, he was in the car. He is hurting my arms. It was flames up here, where he hurt me.
And, my kids came out, my son and my two daughters came out of the kitchen, by the door.
They said: “You can’t assault my dad in the yard.” (The other policeman) took the pepper
spray and sprayed all my kids with the pepper spray.

Commentary
Prosecutors declined to take the Hendricks family’s complaints forward in court.
Dawid Hendricks, on the other hand, is appearing in court on charges of obstructing police
duties and assault.

Commentary
Following a report by investigative journalism unit Viewfinder, police commissioner Khehla
Sitole recently replied to a Parliamentary question that both Gabriels and his former boss,
Athlone station commander Mark Adonis, are now under departmental investigation. Yet,
both remain on the job. Neither responded to our request for their comment.
Previously, Adonis has said that he is waiting for a recommendation from police watchdog
IPID.

Adonis
If IPID sends us a recommendation then there will be an investigation, definitely, if our
members was at fault.

Commentary
But in October last year, the police service issued a circular which countered this common
misconception that station commanders must wait for IPID’s recommendation before acting.
In fact, commanders who failed to act were themselves guilty of misconduct, it read.

Sean Tait
I think that the SAPS management have finally realised and have been finally put under
pressure that they needed to be put in under to begin to address this.
You also need to see from SAPS on what will be done to prevent the repetition of these
cases, [...] the problem is systemic and we need see how it can be fixed.

Commentary
Police spokesperson Major General Mathapelo Peters, to whom our queries were escalated,
did not respond to Carte Blanche’s request for an interview.
Thabo Leholo, IPID’s head in the Western Cape declined an interview request, saying that
Isaacs’ death was still under investigation.

Wasiela Isaacs
I want to see justice. They must come forward and say why did they hit my son like that?
That night, that is my question.

In studio promos:
A notorious police officer in the Western Cape is transferred to the quiet fishing village of
Lamberts Bay. So why has his alleged reign of terror been allowed to continue? (11 seconds)

In South Africa police brutality has become routine. Upsound with subtitles: he took the
pepper spray and sprayed all my kids with the pepper spray. We investigate why one
alleged repeat offender in the police service was allowed to stay on the job. (21 seconds)

In February 2020, Wasiela Isaacs’s son, Adam, died of blunt force trauma injuries after he
was arrested by soldiers and police officers in Athlone. Upsound Wasiela Isaacs: “I was
there by his bedside and I was praying and I was praying that night (crying) that was the
night that he passed away.” Nearly two years later, why has no one been held accountable?
(21 seconds)

Tuesday promos
Arrested for possible drug related violations, why did one man end up dead in the hands of
police in the Western Cape?
“They hit him with a brick” Mac “a brick?”
A joint operation between police and the army in the Western Cape goes horribly wrong -
leaving one man dead, and a mother seeking closure.
"I was there by his bedside and I was praying and I was praying that night. That was the
night that he passed away." (crying)

Ek sien daar het hulle vir Adam. Hulle begin vir Adam te slaat. Dis die army manne, en dis Gabriels hulle. So muur, laat hulle hom daar teen aan staan. Dan kom hulle aan gehardloop, dan trap hulle hom. Now, one kan see through the windscreen. Now I see, here in front of me things are happening. I see there they have Adam. They start beating Adam. It’s the army men, and it is Gabriels and them. There was a wall like this, and they made him stand against it. Then they came running up, and they stomped on him. En soos hulle hom slaat, kom hulle terug na my toe en se jy’s next. (Praying) Allah help my. And, as they are beating him, they came running back to me saying “you’re next.” (Praying indistinctly) I just said: “Allah help me.” Shamiel Gamieldien Daai kollega van Gabriels, hy’t so ‘n baksteen opgetel jong. A baksteen, hy konnie meer se eina of so of se niks nie. Ek hoor hy gooi dit gwa teen daai man se rug. That colleague of Gabriels, the white one, he picked up a brick. A brick. Adam, he couldn’t say “ouch” or cry or anything. He could not feel it anymore. I just heard how he threw it “Gwah!” against that man’s back. Link Watchdog records contain many brutality allegations against officers at Athlone police station. Yet, complainants - such as the family of Adam Isaacs - say they have lost faith in the station commander to discipline officers implicated in these cases. Commentary Following recommendations from the Independent Police Investigative Directorate, criminal prosecutors are currently pursuing convictions in two separate counts of “assault with intent to do grievous bodily harm” against Gabriels. Yet, Athlone station commander Colonel Mark Adonis never gave Gabriels more than a “warning”, in spite of repeat watchdog findings against him. In the end, Adonis’ office also failed to investigate claims that Gabriels and other Athlone officers participated in the torture of Adam Isaacs. Sean Tait is the director of the African Policing Civilian Oversight Forum. Sean Tait Now, I’m familiar with the case of Sergeant Gabriels and the incidents in Athlone. Sean Tait You can say that it's part of the systemic failure within the South African police services when it comes to discipline or when it comes to consequence management. Well we’ve seen a steady decline In discipline cases being processed through the South African Police Services. Sean Tait So a fraction resulting in any form of punitive sanction. Commentary Instead of disciplining and rehabilitating problem officers, Tait says that the police service may simply transfer them to other precincts. Sean Tait When these transfers happen to more rural areas and more remote areas, you also removing the individual from the scrutiny that might been available in a more kind metropolitan or resourced area such as Cape Town. Link In 2020, the police service transferred Sergeant Giovanni Gabriels to this station in the quiet, west-coast fishing village of Lamberts Bay. Here, some community members say, his pattern of assault and abuse continued unchecked. Commentary Dawid Hendricks is a handyman at the Cederberg Municipality. He has accused Sgt Gabriels of attacking him at his home in January last year. MacFarlane Moleli Dawid, just explain to me what happened that night that you say you were assaulted by police. Take me through what happened? David Hendricks My vrou was geroep deur ‘n vriendin van haar… Haar kind is siek en sy het gegaan. Maar dis Covid. Daai tyd was dit die Covid tyd. En sy het gegaan. My wife was called by a friend, whose child was sick, and she went. It was Covid. It was Covid time. But, she did go. En sy het gebel vir my meisiekind, om te s ek moet vir haar kom haal. Toe is dit al oor die curfew-tyd. And, she called my daughter to ask that I should come fetch her. Then it was already after the curfew time. Commentary Dawid says that Gabriels and a colleague were patrolling his street to enforce curfew, when they confronted him. David Hendricks En toe ek nou wil uitklim by my driver kant, hier ruk iemand die deur oop, voor my kombuis deur, ruk hy die deur oop en hy het my in die kar. Ek vra ‘wat maak jy nou? Jy maak my dood. Jy choke my.’ Ek wil opstaan. Ek wil uitklim. En hy is in die kar, hy maak my arms seer, ek was dokter toe met my arms. Ek het ‘n J88. Dis ‘n hele vlamme hier op gewees soos hy vir my seergemaak het. En my drie kinders kom uit, my seun en twee meisiekinders kom uit. By die kombuis uit, dis voor die deur. Hulle s ‘Jy kan nie my pa in yard aanrand nie’. Alan Kotze vat die pepper spray en hy spray al drie my kinders met die pepper spray. And, when I wanted to get out at the driver’s side, someone pulled the door open. In front of my kitchen door, he pulled the door open and he had me in the car. I asked him “What are you doing? You are killing me! You are choking me!” I wanted to stand up. I wanted to get out. And, he was in the car. He is hurting my arms. It was flames up here, where he hurt me. And, my kids came out, my son and my two daughters came out of the kitchen, by the door. They said: “You can’t assault my dad in the yard.” (The other policeman) took the pepper spray and sprayed all my kids with the pepper spray. Commentary Prosecutors declined to take the Hendricks family’s complaints forward in court. Dawid Hendricks, on the other hand, is appearing in court on charges of obstructing police duties and assault. Commentary Following a report by investigative journalism unit Viewfinder, police commissioner Khehla Sitole recently replied to a Parliamentary question that both Gabriels and his former boss, Athlone station commander Mark Adonis, are now under departmental investigation. Yet, both remain on the job. Neither responded to our request for their comment. Previously, Adonis has said that he is waiting for a recommendation from police watchdog IPID. Adonis If IPID sends us a recommendation then there will be an investigation, definitely, if our members was at fault. Commentary But in October last year, the police service issued a circular which countered this common misconception that station commanders must wait for IPID’s recommendation before acting. In fact, commanders who failed to act were themselves guilty of misconduct, it read. Sean Tait I think that the SAPS management have finally realised and have been finally put under pressure that they needed to be put in under to begin to address this. You also need to see from SAPS on what will be done to prevent the repetition of these cases, [...] the problem is systemic and we need see how it can be fixed. Commentary Police spokesperson Major General Mathapelo Peters, to whom our queries were escalated, did not respond to Carte Blanche’s request for an interview. Thabo Leholo, IPID’s head in the Western Cape declined an interview request, saying that Isaacs’ death was still under investigation. Wasiela Isaacs I want to see justice. They must come forward and say why did they hit my son like that? That night, that is my question. In studio promos: A notorious police officer in the Western Cape is transferred to the quiet fishing village of Lamberts Bay. So why has his alleged reign of terror been allowed to continue? (11 seconds) In South Africa police brutality has become routine. Upsound with subtitles: he took the pepper spray and sprayed all my kids with the pepper spray. We investigate why one alleged repeat offender in the police service was allowed to stay on the job. (21 seconds) In February 2020, Wasiela Isaacs’s son, Adam, died of blunt force trauma injuries after he was arrested by soldiers and police officers in Athlone. Upsound Wasiela Isaacs: “I was there by his bedside and I was praying and I was praying that night (crying) that was the night that he passed away.” Nearly two years later, why has no one been held accountable? (21 seconds) Tuesday promos Arrested for possible drug related violations, why did one man end up dead in the hands of police in the Western Cape? “They hit him with a brick” Mac “a brick?” A joint operation between police and the army in the Western Cape goes horribly wrong - leaving one man dead, and a mother seeking closure. "I was there by his bedside and I was praying and I was praying that night. That was the night that he passed away." (crying)

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Did the South African Police Service enable a brutal murder by leaving this problem cop unchecked?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: 18 months long running investigation into repeat violent offender within SAPS, and SAPS management failure to discipline him. Backed up by a longer term investigation of the systemic use of torture and violence in police work in SA and failure of police accountability mechanisms in South Africa i.e. this case study is illustrative of a much deeper and systemic malaise within policing in SA
metadata.Summary: Long term investigation has shown that alleged repeat violent offender within Western Cape SAPS, Sergeant Giovanni Gabriels, was left unchecked by SAPS management. He then led an operation during which a 36-year-old man was fatally assaulted, with witnesses saying Gabriels directed and participated in assault on Adam Isaacs. Documentation and records demonstrate how the officer was consistently shielded from disciplinary action by his superiors, in spite of findings against him.
metadata.Further information: Full rendering of the characters, records available and investigative findings in this story is accessible via a long form article published by Viewfinder and News24: https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/viewfinder-did-saps-enable-a-brutal-murder-by-leaving-this-problem-cop-unpunished-20211201 Further angle: the officer has been transferred to a small community (Lambertsbaai) where his pattern of abuse has apparently continued.
